title: Parametric survival: accelerated failure time
biology: Botanists compare germination timing after control or cold treatment.
design: 140 independent seeds; some remain ungerminated at final follow-up.
question: Does cold treatment stretch the germination-time distribution?
null: The treatment coefficient is zero: the cold/control time ratio is one.
options: exp(coefficient) gives the AFT time ratio
Surv retains seeds that are right-censored
assumptions: A common acceleration factor for treatment
parametric: Check other justified parametric time distributions
Cox changes the effect scale to a hazard ratio
nonparametric: Kaplan–Meier estimates survival without a time distribution

plot_args.note: Separate empirical steps from model curves
Name both groups and line meanings

practice: Would an AFT time ratio above one speed up or delay germination?
code_simulate:
set.seed(2113)
d <- data.frame(seed = 1:140,
                treatment = rep(c("Control", "Cold"), each = 70))
log_scale <- log(20) + .4 * (d$treatment == "Cold")
event_time <- rweibull(140, shape = 1.8, scale = exp(log_scale))
follow_up <- runif(140, 22, 50)
d$days <- pmin(event_time, follow_up)
d$event <- as.integer(event_time <= follow_up)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

code_analysis:
fit <- survival::survreg(survival::Surv(days, event) ~ treatment,
                         data = d, dist = "weibull")
summary(fit)
time_ci <- exp(confint(fit)["treatmentCold", ])
generating_model: 140 independent seeds (70 per group) have Weibull germination times with shape 1.8 and scale exp(log(20) + 0.4 if Cold). Thus control scale is 20 days and cold scale is about 29.84 days. Independent censoring times are Uniform(22, 50) days. Save minimum time and event indicator without rounding.
generating_truth: The population cold/control time ratio is exp(0.4) ≈ 1.492, so the equal-time null is false. The generating Weibull distribution matches the fitted AFT family.
teaching_point: An AFT coefficient becomes a time ratio; it is not interpreted as a Cox hazard ratio.
